Using these quotes, we can put each individual into a microcosm that exists in a macrocosm that is merely a microcosm of exponentially-bigger macrocosms. Just as if the Son breaks the Laws of the Father, there are punishments and consequences, so also does the Father pay punishments to the State when he breaks their laws. What else is the bickering of siblings, but an attempt from special interest demographics to get the legislature (Parents) to take their side, reduced to the microcosm-level of individuals?

Accordingly, every season I have my S.O. make up a list for review of the needs we will need for that season. Consider it the business equivalent of writing up a projected quarterly budget. From there, on a monthly basis, I write up a monthly budget to ensure that every nickel is accounted for. Anything that is leftover (assuming we found ways to cut costs during the month) gets put half-into Savings and half-into Leisure Savings (basically, saving up for extravagant activities. Possibly a cruise, multiweek vacation, etc.)

I made a comparison earlier to the Legislative branch of government. In that vein, I function as the House, whereas the S.O. functions as the Senate. I hold power over finances and expenditures, whereas the S.O. has power over matters domestic, as upkeep of the home falls under her domain. Judicial branch is covered by a bicameral effort to decide the best course forward, with occassional debate using the adversarial system. No judge, as reliance on the rules of argument is based on an honor system, where noncompliance is penalized by an automatic forfeit and ceasing of argumentation. (In short, the one who didn't violate the rules of debate walks away, and the other side is considered to forfeit the argument) I, of course, operate as Executive Branch, with veto ability (to be used sparingly).

I find that in both partners having their own sphere of influence in the household (Government) with a decent separation of powers and responsibility, and with responsible exercise of said power, household matters run generally quite smoothly. Assuming communication is kept open (never been a problem for us), the system largely works to defuse conflict by pointing it out before it gets too large to handle, via the Legislative process.

It should go without saying that I do this with a Significant Other that was also raised in a somewhat traditional and conservative home. I am also in a State that disregards the concept of Commonlaw Marriages. I make no guarantees on how this may or may not work, especially if attempted with one of the more "liberated" girls that has little respect for precedent or tradition. I can only say what has worked for me, for these 9 years, and however longer we may last. Remember, she's not yours...it's just your turn.
